column1: # tests/workable_items/remint_branch_equivalents.tsv -- equivalence register of the remint branch sweep
# (tests/workable_items/remint_branch_sweep.py, round 5, R4-2). One line per surviving mutant that is
# proven equivalent: <key as printed by --list> TAB <reason>. A survivor without a line here fails the
# sweep, and a line whose key no longer names a branch fails it too (a stale entry).

column2: Equivalent: every caller of Rewriter.text passes a str (norm() of a column, the literal "none", or the text of a file), so the only input the guard catches is the empty string; with the guard forced off, "" is split into one empty line, no pattern matches it, and the method returns ("", 0), the same value the guard returns.

Equivalent: the expression is reached only when close() found evidence (`ev` non-empty), and closure_evidence returns a non-empty value only from a row whose event_type is in CLOSURE_EVENTS; that same row is in `cl`, so `cl` is never empty there and forcing the test True changes nothing.

Equivalent: `word` is either status_word(ts) under t_term (in CLOSE_STATUS by the definition of t_term) or the event_type of the last row of a non-empty `cl` (in CLOSURE_EVENTS, which is set(CLOSE_STATUS)); the refusal is a guard no input reaches, so forcing the test False changes nothing.

Equivalent: every new id is the prefix and an ASCII number start+k, start being one more than the largest number among the target ids that fully match the prefix pattern; a target id equal to a new id would itself match that pattern with a larger number, a contradiction, so the test is always False.

Equivalent: forced True, the own add passes "--created-by=" with an empty value where the code omits the flag; the engine's --created-by defaults to '' (its add --help), and the remint suite's case "engine fact: an empty --created-by= and --assigned-to= equal omitting them" checks on every run that the stored item, its history row and its segment are the same either way.

Equivalent: forced True, the own add passes "--assigned-to=" with an empty value where the code omits the flag; the engine's --assigned-to defaults to '' (its add --help), and the remint suite's case "engine fact: an empty --created-by= and --assigned-to= equal omitting them" checks on every run that the stored item, its history row and its segment are the same either way.

Equivalent: v_split splits on a pattern with one capturing group, so re.split returns 2k+1 pieces for k ids and the skeleton (the even pieces) has exactly one piece more than the token list; the test is reached only after sk_w == sk_g, so len(tk_w) == len(sk_w) - 1 == len(sk_g) - 1 == len(tk_g) and the branch can never be taken. The remint suite case "v_split fact: a skeleton has one piece more than its id tokens" checks the fact on every run (ten texts, with a control that the split finds both ids of a list).

column2: Equivalent: forced True, verify also calls check_od for an own item that has no obsolete_details row on either side; check_od returns at once when both rows are None (its first test is false, its second returns), so nothing is appended. The remint suite case "check_od fact: no row on either side appends nothing" checks this on every run, with a control that a row on one side only is reported.
